target.title: fix(snapshot): propagate lock failures instead of empty lists
target.body:
## Summary

`snapshotDirectoryURLs` treated lock failures as an empty snapshot list. Callers such as `listSnapshots` and clean paths then looked like "no snapshots exist" when the real problem was inability to lock snapshot state.

## Problem

```swift
} catch {
    self.logger.error("Failed to lock snapshot state for directory read: \(error)")
    return []
}
```

Empty storage and lock failure both returned `[]`. Operators and agents could delete nothing, list nothing, or assume a clean cache when snapshot storage was actually unusable.

## Change

- Make `snapshotDirectoryURLs` throw `SnapshotError.storageError` on lock failure.
- Update `listSnapshots`, `cleanSnapshotsOlderThan`, and `cleanAllSnapshots` (already `throws`) to use `try`.
- Add regression tests and a standalone proof script.

True empty storage (lock succeeds, directory empty) still returns `[]` via the success path.

## Failure scenario

1. Snapshot storage path cannot open the invalidation lock file (missing parents, permissions, etc.).
2. `listSnapshots()` / clean APIs call `snapshotDirectoryURLs`.
3. Pre-fix: returns success with zero items (looks empty).
4. Post-fix: throws `SnapshotError.storageError("Failed to lock snapshot state...")`.

## Origin

Introduced in commit `4f2b0e9cb` (2026-06-13, Peter Steinberger) with the implicit-latest invalidation lock work (~20 days on main).

## Related

- Same "mask failure as empty success" class as merged [#209](https://github.com/openclaw/Peekaboo/pull/209) and [#210](https://github.com/openclaw/Peekaboo/pull/210).
- Lock helper `withImplicitLatestInvalidationLock` already throws on `open`/`flock` failure; only this caller swallowed it into `[]`.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Snapshot directory listing mapped lock failures to an empty array, indistinguishable from a storage that simply had no snapshots.

**Real environment tested:** macOS arm64, Swift Command Line Tools, Peekaboo worktree at `baef3be1` + this patch.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```console
$ swiftc -parse-as-library -o /tmp/prove-snapshot-lock \
    scripts/prove-snapshot-lock-failure.swift && /tmp/prove-snapshot-lock
=== Unfixed lock failure ===
success count=0 (looks like empty storage)
=== Fixed lock failure ===
failure: Storage error: Failed to lock snapshot state for directory read: No such file or directory
=== Fixed empty storage (lock ok) ===
success count=0 (true empty)
PROOF PASS
```

Also built the production target:

```console
$ swift build --package-path Core/PeekabooAutomationKit --target PeekabooAutomationKit
Build of target: 'PeekabooAutomationKit' complete!
```

**Evidence after fix:** Terminal output above. Unfixed lock failure reports success with count 0; fixed reports `SnapshotError.storageError`; true empty storage still succeeds with count 0.

**Observed result after fix:** Lock failures propagate as storage errors through the existing throwing public APIs; empty storage remains a successful empty list.

**What was not tested:** Full XCTest/`Testing` package run on this machine (CLT only; no Xcode.app). `SnapshotDirectoryLockFailureTests` is included for CI/Xcode runners.

## Test plan

- [x] `swift build --package-path Core/PeekabooAutomationKit --target PeekabooAutomationKit`
- [x] Standalone `scripts/prove-snapshot-lock-failure.swift` (PROOF PASS)
- [ ] CI: `SnapshotDirectoryLockFailureTests` (missing storage path => throws; existing empty dir => empty list)
